children: Amid a string of big-ticket sales on Nantucket, a historic home overlooking Nantucket Harbor has sold for $42.5 million, a record for the affluent island off the coast of Massachusetts.

The sellers of the Brant Point property are members of the Fife family, who have owned the home since 1972. The property wasn't on the public market at the time of the sale and the buyer's identity couldn't be determined. The Fifes declined to comment.

Built in the 1930s, the house is located on Hulbert Avenue, an oceanfront stretch with multimillion-dollar beach properties. Set on 0.62 acres, the roughly 6,400-square-foot house has eight bedrooms and direct beach and harbor access.
Barbara Fife was New York City's deputy mayor for planning and development from 1990 to 1993. Her husband, investor Martin Fife, died in 2004.

The deal narrowly surpasses the Nantucket record, set in 2023 when Barstool Sports founder, Dave Portnoy, paid $42 million for a waterfront compound. The Massachusetts record was set this summer with the $43 million sale of a compound on Martha's Vineyard.

The closing is just one of several eight-figure deals on the island in recent weeks. Last month, a nearby home sold for the third time since 2022 — this time for $35 million, up from $26 million in 2024 and $19.9 million in 2022.

Brant Point is an iconic waterfront neighborhood visible to boats entering and exiting Nantucket Harbor. Expensive homes surround the centuries-old Brant Point Lighthouse, one of the island's most recognizable landmarks.
The listing agent for the Fife property was Jeanne Hicks of Lee Real Estate. Chandra Miller of Maury People Sotheby's International Realty represented the buyer. They declined to comment.

Prices in Nantucket are being driven by high demand and few opportunities to purchase, said Bernadette Meyer of Sotheby's, who was not involved in the Fife deal. She is currently marketing a historic compound downtown asking $34 million. "I don't even think we've seen the tip of the iceberg," she said. "The demand for A-plus quality real estate is insatiable."
